speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: asked the Minister for Health with regard to the recommended strategy by the Interagency Taskforce on Mental Health and Well-being (a) whether the Government will consider elderly mental health as a separate pillar given the increasing proportion and vulnerability of the demographic; and (b) what outcomes and indicators are being set for the work of the Taskforce.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: asked the Minister for Health whether the Ministry can provide an update on the Interagency Taskforce on Mental Health and Well-being, especially on its plans to improve mental health literacy among citizens and create an inclusive society for persons with mental health conditions.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) what recourse is available to caregivers of elderly care recipients when the latter exhibit self-harm or aggressive behaviours which require emergency interventions; (b) whether the restructured hospitals, including the Institute of Mental Health, are equipped to handle these cases; and (c) how can geriatricians and social service agencies play a role in such case management.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The task force's recommendations are aimed at creating a caring and inclusive society, where all can seek help and be supported to achieve mental health and well-being, and can participate meaningfully in our society.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The first focus area is improving accessibility, coordination and quality of mental health services.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The second is strengthening of services and support for youths' mental well-being.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And the third is improving workplace well-being measures and employment support.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: For our youths, we want to promote the positive use of technology and social media and propose to develop a parents' toolbox to enable parents to better support their children's socioemotional well-being.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: At the workplace, we propose to improve mental well-being support systems and work-life harmony strategies and equip employers with knowledge on supporting persons with mental health needs.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: In addition, there is a need to improve access to vocational training and increase job opportunities for persons with mental health conditions.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: To promote mental health awareness and literacy in the population, the Health Promotion Board (HPB) launched the national campaign in October 2021 titled "It’s OKAY to Reach Out".

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The campaign aims to normalise discussions about and increase understanding of mental health issues.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The campaign encourages us to reach out for help and, where possible, reach out to provide help.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The campaign includes community dialogue sessions, activity-based workshops and educational webinars where participants learn more about mental well-being and equip themselves with practical coping tips as well as how to reach out to seek support and support others.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: To complement this national campaign, HPB also rolled out MindSG, an online portal featuring resources curated by mental health experts to provide Singaporeans with credible, reliable and convenient access to important relevant content.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: HPB will be launching the second instalment of the "It’s OKAY to Reach Out" national campaign in the coming months.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There are existing mental health services to cater to the needs of persons with mental health conditions and their caregivers.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Caregivers of elderly care recipients, in particular, those who exhibit self-harm or aggressive behaviours, can call the Institute of Mental Health (IMH)'s 24-hour Mental Health Helpline at 6389 2222 to seek help in managing crisis situations.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Where necessary, IMH will also make home visits to provide crisis interventions.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: When the acute psychiatric condition is stabilised, the elderly care recipients may be referred for follow-up at the outpatient clinics at the restructured hospitals where their care would be overseen by healthcare professionals trained in mental health, including psycho-geriatricians.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: In the community, the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) has worked with social service agencies to set up community intervention teams which can provide further support for these elderly care recipients through psychosocial therapeutic intervention and counselling.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The first is on my question about the focus on the elderly.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am very appreciative of the three focus areas as well as the 12 recommendations that we are seeking consultations on.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, in 2020, we saw the highest number of elderly suicides since 1991.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While in 2021, the number has gone down slightly, it remains to be seen what the future might hold.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In any case, the vocabulary around elderly mental health is much less socialised.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Many still consider it very taboo and I think —

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin, please ask your question.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: So, my question is, will the task force consider focusing, as a special focus area, on the elderly's mental health and their caregivers as well?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: The second part is, I appreciate focus area 1, but I think we need to be realistic that in order to have better access, quality and coordination of these services, we also need to have more resources because AIC and other agencies tend to be really overstretched.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: All the good work that is done in support —

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin, ask your question, please.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: Does the task force plan on providing more manpower and resources, other than just raising literacy and providing education?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But I think we have to start at getting the strategy and systems in place first.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Then, the task force will move on to other subtasks following on from that.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Indeed, it is important to consider the needs of and support for the elderly who have mental health illnesses and those of their caregivers.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The first is that for the seniors' mental health, we need to look at it a little bit differently partly because they often have concomitant, associated chronic health conditions.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Both need to be dealt with together, holistically.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, it is a combined mental and health approach.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: That is what the professionals have been doing already.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Which is the second point, that is, that there are resources that are available, there are professionals working in this space.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I mentioned the psycho-geriatricians and the other teams in my earlier answer.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The third point is that some of the efforts that we are making around the larger strategy of mental health will directly improve access to, and services for, the elderly, for example, the extent to which we are looking at the community care providers to bring some of these services closer to home, including, for example, eldercare centres.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I hear the efforts by the interagency task force in reaching out and getting this.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: My question is, for those who are not reaching out, are there plans to increase these nodes or networks to allow them to be, in a way, screened or detected, so that we can prevent issues in terms of mental health?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, that is very much part of our strategy.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Apart from calling the hotline for remote assistance, sometimes, they will choose to go to IMH.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Related to that, sometimes, caregivers may feel that it is more expeditious to send the elderly to a nearby restructured hospital because, if there is self-harm, there may be personal danger.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: They may feel that it is safer to send the elderly to those settings.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: So, are restructured hospitals equipped to support such instances?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The issue of dealing with an elderly patient who has a mental health condition and who then has a caregiver requiring assistance to deal with that situation, there is not a single solution – just as there is not a single archetype or a single set of challenges.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Indeed, the helpline is there for advice as well as to coordinate onward referral.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Indeed, the family, the caregiver, can bring the senior to IMH if that is where they think the mental health condition is best dealt with and they can bring them to the restructured hospitals which are also equipped to deal with vulnerable persons, persons who are entirely dependent and people with acute mental health conditions deteriorating.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The restructured hospitals and their emergency departments are equipped.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: At the beginning, the Member talked about IMH being the first port of call.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: One of the things that we are looking at within the task force is to perhaps shift that perception that IMH has to both be the first port of call as well as the only port of call.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: That is part of what the task force is going to try and do.
